title: Rethinking Access Control for AI Agents: Recent Advances and Open Challenges
abstract: arXiv:2611.06764v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model agents access data, invoke tools, and act on users' behalf. Keeping these actions within authorized bounds is challenging because agents choose their own execution paths while permissions and operating conditions may change. This paper surveys recent advances in agent access control across four areas: policy specification and derivation, identity and delegation, action and resource enforcement, and information flow control. We compare their control objects, enforcement boundaries, and assumptions to examine what individual mechanisms achieve and how they can work together. Building on this analysis, we rethink four aspects of authorization: plan selection shapes permission requirements; contextual information can inform decisions without itself granting authority; restrictions must retain their meaning across system interfaces; and authorization must be reassessed as workflows evolve. translated_title: 重新思考AI智能体的访问控制：最新进展与开放挑战
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型智能体可以访问数据、调用工具并代表用户执行操作。确保这些行为保持在授权范围内具有挑战性，因为智能体会自行选择执行路径，而权限和运行条件也可能随时变化。本文从四个领域综述了智能体访问控制的最新进展：策略规范与推导、身份与委托、动作与资源执行，以及信息流控制。我们比较了各机制的控制对象、执行边界和前提假设，以审视单个机制所能实现的功能及其协同工作的方式。基于这一分析，我们重新思考了授权的四个方面：计划选择决定了权限需求；上下文信息可以为决策提供依据，但其本身并不授予权限；限制必须在系统接口之间保持其含义；并且随着工作流的演变，必须对授权进行重新评估。这些见解引出了该领域的开放性挑战。
tldr: 本文系统综述了AI智能体访问控制在策略规范、身份委托、动作执行和信息流控制四大领域的最新进展，并重新思考了授权机制的四个核心方面，指出了未来亟待解决的开放性挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper surveys recent advances in access control for AI agents across four areas—policy specification, identity and delegation, action enforcement, and information flow control—and rethinks four key aspects of authorization, highlighting open challenges in this emerging field.
